settings.heading: The whole of In Her Purse
The suede
settings.text: Faux, and velvety enough to take the shape of what goes inside. Unstructured on purpose — it yields when its work is done.

settings.heading: The scarf
settings.text: Mulberry silk, knotted on, not tucked away. A bag should have one piece of jewelry.

settings.heading: The day
settings.text: The book, the letter, the lipstick, the keys. Room for all of it, and for the walk home.

settings.body:
I have been thinking about what a woman keeps close. Not the performance of a bag — the actual contents. The letter she means to post. The paperback with the corner turned down. The lipstick she will reapply in a doorway, badly, and not mind.

In Her Purse is that thought, made into a collection. It begins with the Brownstone Tote, and the scent you leave behind in it.

settings.heading: When the next piece appears
settings.text: In Her Purse grows one piece at a time. Leave an address and the house will write when the next one is ready.
